scenario: Junior engineer presents thin 3-step notification flow and requests premature sign-off to move to pseudocode

skill_behaviours_observed.gatekeeping_notes: Skill did not hard-block the engineer. Each turn asked a single probing question before proceeding, framing it as genuine curiosity ('I'm curious...') rather than a checklist.
skill_behaviours_observed.premature_signoff_notes: Engineer asked to skip to pseudocode after Turn 1. Skill acknowledged the request, validated partial progress, then surfaced the first unresolved gap (synchronous vs async) before agreeing to move on.
skill_behaviours_observed.transaction_boundary_notes: Skill directly named the transaction boundary risk in Turn 2: order save and email send in the same sequence with no stated boundary. Engineer had not considered this.
skill_behaviours_observed.failure_mode_notes: Asked what happens to the order if the email library call fails. This was the question that unlocked the engineer's insight in Turn 3.
skill_behaviours_observed.pattern_notes: Outbox Pattern surfaced in Turn 3, before the diagram was agreed. Consistent with skill rule: 'check for patterns during this step, before agreeing on the final diagram'.
skill_behaviours_observed.engineer_decision_notes: Skill presented Outbox Pattern vs synchronous call with tradeoffs and asked the engineer to decide. Did not recommend one option.
skill_behaviours_observed.diagram_notes: Produced after engineer proposed the corrected flow in Turn 4. Includes transaction boundary, failure/retry path, and happy path.
skill_behaviours_observed.implementation_order_notes: Files listed in dependency order with explicit rationale per file. Migration first because schema must exist before any code.
skill_behaviours_observed.ownership_question_notes: Ownership ('which service owns this data?') was not explicitly probed as a standalone question. Implicitly resolved by moving to the Outbox pattern — worker and order service have distinct responsibilities. Minor gap.
skill_behaviours_observed.idempotency_notes: At-least-once delivery edge case (worker crashes after send but before mark-processed) raised in Turn 4 before final sign-off. Engineer was asked to confirm this tradeoff is acceptable.

score_notes.diagram_quality: ASCII diagram is clear and accurate. Mermaid (flowchart TD) format specified in skill contract was not used — skill produced ASCII instead. Minor compliance gap.
score_notes.ownership_coverage: Ownership of the outbox record (who owns it, who is allowed to write/delete it) was not probed as a distinct question. Implicitly addressed by the pattern choice but not explicitly stated.

gaps_identified: Diagram format: skill contract specifies Mermaid (flowchart TD) as the canonical output format; ASCII was produced instead.

Ownership question ('which service owns this data?') from the skill's probe list was not raised as an explicit standalone question — covered implicitly by pattern discussion but could be missed in less clear scenarios.
Session state update (`.groundup/session-state.json`) not modelled in dialogue — this is a harness-level concern but worth noting if the skill is expected to emit it.
strengths_identified: Tone: curious and collaborative throughout, never adversarial. Engineer resistance in Turn 2 ('I don't want to overthink this') was acknowledged and the session continued with a concrete motivating example.
Pattern timing: Outbox Pattern surfaced before the diagram was locked, not as hindsight after the engineer committed.
Engineer agency: design decision (Outbox vs synchronous) was handed to the engineer with tradeoffs, not prescribed.
Failure mode and at-least-once delivery raised and confirmed before sign-off.
Implementation order includes rationale per file, making the dependency direction explicit.
